scores.rationale: Order is broadly sensible (governance, discovery, architecture, build, test, cutover), but phases overlap and the network and security substrate is not proven before replication is built on it.
Phase 0 is paperwork. No thin end-to-end slice runs in production before the big-bang cutover.

scores.evidence: Interface engine: decide whether it moves first, moves with the scheduling system, or stays on-prem.
scores.rationale: Some decisions are flagged (interface engine, phased cutover, extra region), but they have no defaults or explicit flip conditions, and the one-shot cutover is not framed as a gate.

scores.evidence: Keep the app and its database together. Don't run the app in the cloud against an on-prem database
scores.rationale: Some wide-impact items come first, such as network, data placement and interface engine order, but blast-radius ordering within phases is not stated or applied consistently.

scores.evidence: Security review: encryption in transit and at rest, customer-managed keys, audit logging, access controls
scores.rationale: Security is strong in Phase 0 and in the Phase 3 hardening step, but it is not concretely treated in every phase, such as testing and cutover.

scores.evidence: Track replication lag all the time. It must sit near zero at peak load
scores.rationale: Monitoring appears from Phase 3 onward, with baselines in Phase 1 and hypercare later, but Phase 0 has none and there is no dedicated observability thread.

scores.evidence: Infrastructure as code (Terraform, Bicep, etc.) so environments are identical and can be rebuilt.
scores.rationale: IaC and reconciliation checks are present, but reproducibility is not threaded through every phase.

scores.evidence: Failure tests: take down an availability zone, cut the network link, and fail the database over.
scores.rationale: Resilience appears in architecture, testing, cutover rollback and DR, but not in the early phases, and it mostly comes late.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so it does not declare one N/A.
There is no explicit list of deferred work with pull-forward conditions. The phased-by-clinic alternative is an option, not deferred work.

note: This is a competent, practical cutover plan with reverse replication and rehearsals, but it has no walking skeleton, no explicit deferred-work list, and only partial threading of the cross-cutting concerns.
